recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit as the reconciliation for FHIR-34068. No core source follow-up is needed for this issue; future DiagnosticReport.supportingInfo or genomics IG guidance changes should remain on their own Jira tracks.
issue_request: FHIR-34068 was a Published FHIR-core DiagnosticReport change request resolved as Persuasive with Modification for R5. Clinical Genomics needed DiagnosticReport to refer generically to DocumentReference resources for generated files such as VCFs; OO decided to broaden DiagnosticReport.media from image-only wording to image-or-data wording, update media.comment, and adjust local media guidance.
initial_application: The Jira comment records application via commit e041968cbe8b6a3343953f751b2b5f6f0cc11567 from HL7/fhir#1507. That commit changed source/diagnosticreport/structuredefinition-DiagnosticReport.xml and source/diagnosticreport/diagnosticreport-introduction.xml to use image-or-data wording while retaining DiagnosticReport.media.link as Reference(DocumentReference).
additional_context: DiagnosticReport is active in source/fhir.ini. FHIR-19734 is the earlier same-change-family issue confirming DiagnosticReport.media.link should allow DocumentReference and was fixed in R5. FHIR-48391 later added DocumentReference to DiagnosticReport.supportingInfo.reference for a separate R6 supporting-information use case without reversing FHIR-34068. Clinical Genomics Zulip discussion and OO minutes align with broadening R5 DiagnosticReport.media as the long-term core path.
reconciliation: No source files were changed. Current combined-branch source contains the requested media, media.comment, media.link, and introduction wording; media.link targets DocumentReference; R5 published diagnosticreport.profile.json exposes the same media wording; and a targeted stale-text search found no remaining active image-only DiagnosticReport media labels in source/diagnosticreport.

related_jiras.note: Earlier Applied issue confirming DiagnosticReport.media.link should allow DocumentReference; it explains why FHIR-34068 could focus on broadening the media wording rather than changing the link target.
Later Applied R6 issue adding DocumentReference to DiagnosticReport.supportingInfo.reference for a separate supporting-information use case; it does not supersede or conflict with FHIR-34068.
